headline: Shared filesystem and broad egress create medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks; no documented hard isolation between Plandex and Semantic Kernel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plandex reads/writes a project directory and uses a plan-local sandbox, while Semantic Kernel can consume application-defined files and MCP/OpenAPI tools. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if Plandex outputs are fed into SK plugins or prompts. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Plandex outputs are copied into Semantic Kernel prompts or plugin inputs without sanitization, injection is plausible.
IF Semantic Kernel is configured to treat file or tool output as trusted instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer behavior.
mitigations: Disable auto-ingest of Plandex-generated text into SK prompts.
Add a strict delimiter/template around any transferred content.
Require manual review before SK executes plugin calls from Plandex output.
Log and diff all cross-agent handoffs for provenance.
requires-engineering: add content provenance tags between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read files and send data to external model providers; Plandex touches source code and SK handles application context plus plugin credentials. If they share a workspace or memory store, sensitive code or context can flow to third-party APIs through either agent. The shared-state pathways are documented, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or memory store, source code and application context can be exposed across the pair.
IF either agent forwards retrieved file contents to a hosted model provider, leakage extends beyond the local environment.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and memory stores per agent.
Turn off automatic file-content upload where possible.
Restrict SK plugins to least-privilege credentials.
Review outbound API destinations for both agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex can execute shell commands, write the filesystem, and modify git state; Semantic Kernel can write the filesystem and invoke MCP/OpenAPI tools. If both operate on the same repo or mutable resource, concurrent writes and action overlap can corrupt state or overwrite changes. The profiles show no locking mechanism, so the safer high severity applies.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git repository or directory, write conflicts can occur.
IF SK tools are granted write-capable plugins while Plandex auto-applies changes, concurrent mutation risk increases.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent.
Disable auto-apply in Plandex during SK runs.
Serialize write operations with a manual lock file.
Limit SK plugins to read-only during shared sessions.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex is a planner that stages changes, and Semantic Kernel is a kernel-plus-plugins orchestrator that can act on agent outputs. If SK consumes Plandex plans as authoritative without verification, planning mistakes can cascade into incorrect tool calls or writes. Because the pairwise handoff is plausible but not documented as automatic, medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel uses Plandex output as direct tool-call arguments, errors can propagate without review.
IF Plandex generates incorrect facts that SK then executes, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require a human or rule-based verification step between agents.
Compare Plandex output against source files before acting.
Constrain SK to read-only validation on first pass.
Use structured schemas for handoff messages.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare a residency or certification mismatch. The only concrete compliance-relevant difference is that Plandex handles source code while Semantic Kernel handles application context and plugin credentials, but no PHI/EU-only data class or retention conflict is stated. With insufficient evidence, keep this low rather than infer a breach.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either agent, compliance review becomes necessary.
IF the two agents are deployed under different retention or residency policies, a mismatch may arise.
mitigations: Confirm both agents share the same retention policy.
Avoid placing regulated data in shared workspaces.
Document data-class handling for each agent.
Review plugin/vendor terms before enabling sensitive data flows.
